parameters.note: Sheridan Creek is a small east-slope Carson Range stream near the community of Sheridan in Carson Valley, Douglas County, Nevada (OSM way 824749664; NDOW waters database lists it as Region Western, County Douglas, Type of water Creek or Stream). It drains east — away from the Lake Tahoe basin, over the Carson Range crest — into the Carson River system, so it is NOT a Lake Tahoe tributary and the California §7.50(b) Tahoe-tributary closure and the CR 25-16 'Lake Tahoe and tributaries' listing do not apply. It is a Nevada water governed by NDOW. Sheridan Creek is not separately named in CR 25-16's Douglas County listing (only Lake Tahoe, Spooner Lake, Topaz Lake, and the Douglas County Community Fishing Ponds are broken out) and is not among the Douglas County closed waters, so NDOW's Douglas County general 'All waters' rule applies: open year around.

candidates.summary: Open year-round (Nevada Western Region / Douglas County general 'All waters' regulation; Sheridan Creek is not a separately listed exception or a closed water).

parameters.note: Douglas County general 'All waters' rule allows fishing any hour of the day or night. (The restricted 1-hour-before-sunrise-to-2-hours-after-sunset window in CR 25-16 applies to Lake Tahoe, Spooner Lake, and Topaz Lake specifically — not to this creek.)

candidates.summary: Fishing permitted any hour of the day or night.

parameters.counting_rule: Douglas County general limit: for trout, 5 daily and 10 in possession (possession = two times the daily limit). The full 'All waters' row also allows 5 mountain whitefish and 15 warmwater game fish per day (of which not more than 5 black bass and 5 walleye), but NDOW documents no fishery or fish species for Sheridan Creek, so no water-specific sub-limit applies.

candidates.summary: Nevada Douglas County general limit: 5 trout per day / 10 in possession (plus 5 mountain whitefish and 15 warmwater game fish per day under the general 'All waters' row).

parameters.note: Nevada requires a fishing license for anglers 12 years of age and older (residents and nonresidents); a nonresident under 12 may fish without a license but is limited to 50% of the daily creel and possession limits. Because this is a Nevada water and not Lake Tahoe, the Lake Tahoe CA/NV license reciprocity does not apply — a Nevada fishing license is required.

candidates.summary: Nevada fishing license required for anglers 12 and older.
